entries.description: Which digest DataHashing computes. MD5 and SHA-1 are the weak ones a signature from an older service still asks for. SHA-256 is the one to use when the choice is open.

entries.signature: New DataHashing(algorithm : HashFunction [, key : BinaryData | string])
entries.description:
A digest built from the bytes handed to Append. Without a key it is MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256. With a key it is the HMAC of that algorithm: the key is a BinaryData, or a string read as UTF-8.

Append takes a BinaryData, or a string read as UTF-8. An empty piece adds nothing. HashSum is the digest as a BinaryData. Reading it finishes the calculation: a second read returns the same bytes, and a further Append is refused. New DataHashing() with no algorithm is refused.
entries.parameters:
algorithm — a HashFunction value.
key — optional. Present, the sum is an HMAC.

entries.description: Adds bytes to the digest. A string is read as UTF-8. A BinaryData is taken as it is. After HashSum has been read, Append is refused.
entries.parameters: data — a BinaryData, or a string.

entries.description: The digest. Reading it finishes the calculation. A second read returns the same bytes. Nothing can be appended after it.
